input.question: Why does it take hours to install big programs and games but seconds to uninstall it?
input.ground_truth: When you are installing a game, you are writing the files to your hard drive. It has to remember where to access those files. The uninstallation is just forgetting those locations on your drive, not actually erasing them.

Question: Why does it take hours to install big programs and games but seconds to uninstall it?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big box of LEGO bricks. When you want to build something big with all the bricks, it takes a long time because you have to find every single brick, put them in the right place, and make sure everything fits just right.

But when you want to put all the LEGO bricks back into the box, you just dump them in. It goes really fast because you don’t have to be careful or find the right spot for each brick.

Installing a big program or game is like building with LEGO—it takes time because the computer has to put lots of little pieces in the right place. Uninstalling is like putting the LEGO bricks back in the box—it’s quicker because the computer just takes everything away without worrying about the details.
